round1_to_round2.independence_verdict: Mostly anchoring on the facts, partly independent on comps. Evidence: all five agents copied my round-1 net debt of about $175M and my '$140M 2030 notes remaining'. Both were wrong: the 2030 notes had $200M of principal, not $300M, so $40M remains and net debt is about $76M. Agents 1 and 2 said they had verified these figures in the 2026-07-17 8-K. That 8-K does not give the remaining principal, but it does say the exchange issued about 8.7M new shares, and no agent noticed. On comps the agents did re-pull Nasdaq/Zacks data themselves, and their sets differ (10-11 names, with or without TTMI/BHE/MU). But all of them reused the same stale Zacks JBL figure, so their core medians moving to about 19x is shared error, not independent confirmation. The fair-value convergence on about $61 mostly reflects my round-1 multiple framing (16x NTM-at-horizon EPS) being adopted.

revision_check.new_facts_checked: The new 25%-weight 'precedent transaction' leg ($62.4 per as-converted share from SK hynix) is not a valid fair-value method for the common. (2) It was signed on 2026-07-27, when PENG closed at $52.49 (the 07-28 close was $48.13), so it is a 19% premium for those features, not a mark of common value. Use it as evidence of strategic interest and a reduced overhang, with 0-10% weight at most. Dropping it changes agent 5's FV by only about -$0.3.

disagreements.topic: Net debt after the July 2026 refinancing (my round-1 error, copied by all five agents)
disagreements.positions: All agents now use $175-176M principal net debt, with about $140M of 2030 notes remaining (from my round-1 file). An independent SEC fact-check says the 2030 notes were $200M originally.
disagreements.resolution: Corrected to about $76M. The 10-Q states '$200.0 million in aggregate principal amount of 2030 Notes were outstanding' at 2026-05-29 (my round-1 '$300M' was wrong). $160.0M was exchanged, leaving $40.0M. Debt principal = $750M 2031 + $14.5M 2029 + $40.0M 2030 = $804.5M. Pro forma cash = $440.3M + $735.1M - $136.7M - $161.4M - $49.1M - $100M = $728.2M, before Q4 cash flow. The $100M repaid was a revolver borrowing under the JPMorgan 2025 Credit Agreement, not a term loan (10-Q: 'we borrowed $100.0 million under the 2025 Credit Facility', a $400M revolving facility).

disagreements.resolution: The 8-K says the exchange consideration was $136.7M cash plus about 4.7M shares for $135.5M of 2029 notes, and $161.4M cash plus about 4.0M shares for $160.0M of 2030 notes. That is about 8.7M new shares, so basic is about 59.9M (51.24M on the 10-Q cover of 2026-07-02 + 8.7M) and as-converted about 66.0M with the preferred, before about 1M net excess shares on the remaining notes. Market cap at $61.36 is about $3.68B on basic shares, not $3.14B. This dilution was already largely in the treasury-method diluted count before the exchange (the notes were net-share settled and deep in the money), so P/E legs on consensus non-GAAP EPS are broadly unaffected. EV legs are overstated by about $7-8 a share. A residual risk: if any FY27 model still uses the 56M FY26 share guide, EPS is about 10% too high. The Oct-6 print will reveal the Q4 diluted count.

JBL: the Zacks FY Aug-27 figure of $15.69 (4 analysts) is stale. JBL has reported FY26 ($13.09), and the S&P Global consensus updated 2026-10-01 is FY27 $17.69 (range $17.49-18.03) and FY28 $22.17. CY27 = 8/12 x 17.69 + 4/12 x 22.17 = $19.18, so 15.9x at $304.41, not 17.5-18.7x. NTAP, PLXS and TTMI do not belong in the median. NTAP is a software- and subscription-heavy storage franchise with about 70% gross margin. PLXS and TTMI are A&D/healthcare-heavy EMS and PCB/RF names whose 21-31x multiples reflect defense and low-cyclicality re-ratings; they are also defense names, which is irrelevant to a memory-pass-through systems company. With them the median is 20.5x, which is inflated.
